chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Dawud al-Munshid, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'All water is pure until one knows that it is impure.'

key_terms.طَاهِرٌ: tahir — ritually pure, in the state required for valid worship
key_terms.قَذِرٌ: najas (qadhir) — ritually impure, contaminated; a legal status that invalidates worship
key_terms.يُعْلَمَ: certain knowledge — the legal threshold for changing the presumption of purity

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about the purity of water according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes one of the foundational principles of Islamic jurisprudence: the presumption of purity (tahara) for water. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) taught that water in its natural state is considered ritually clean unless there is definite knowledge of contamination. This ruling provided the Shia Muslim community with a practical legal principle rooted in the broader jurisprudential maxim that certainty is not overturned by doubt.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Dawood Al Munshid, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Yunus, from Hammad Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The water, all of it is (to be considered as) clean, until one knows that it is dirty’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from abu Dawud al-Munshid from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from Yunus from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, that
all water (from source) is clean until it is found out that it is not clean.”
